{"arxiv_id":"2409.18374v1","arxiv_url":"http://arxiv.org/abs/2409.18374v1","title":"Adaptive Learning of the Latent Space of Wasserstein Generative
  Adversarial Networks","authors":["Yixuan Qiu","Qingyi Gao","Xiao Wang"],"published_date":"2024-09-27T01:25:22Z","journal":"","doi":"","summary":"Generative models based on latent variables, such as generative adversarial
networks (GANs) and variational auto-encoders (VAEs), have gained lots of
interests due to their impressive performance in many fields. However, many
data such as natural images usually do not populate the ambient Euclidean space
but instead reside in a lower-dimensional manifold. Thus an inappropriate
choice of the latent dimension fails to uncover the structure of the data,
possibly resulting in mismatch of latent representations and poor generative
qualities. Towards addressing these problems, we propose a novel framework
called the latent Wasserstein GAN (LWGAN) that fuses the Wasserstein
auto-encoder and the Wasserstein GAN so that the intrinsic dimension of the
data manifold can be adaptively learned by a modified informative latent
distribution. We prove that there exist an encoder network and a generator
network in such a way that the intrinsic dimension of the learned encoding
distribution is equal to the dimension of the data manifold. We theoretically
establish that our estimated intrinsic dimension is a consistent estimate of
the true dimension of the data manifold. Meanwhile, we provide an upper bound
on the generalization error of LWGAN, implying that we force the synthetic data
distribution to be similar to the real data distribution from a population
perspective. Comprehensive empirical experiments verify our framework and show
that LWGAN is able to identify the correct intrinsic dimension under several
scenarios, and simultaneously generate high-quality synthetic data by sampling
from the learned latent distribution.","github_url":"https://github.com/yixuan/LWGAN","main_contributions":"The paper introduces the Latent Wasserstein GAN (LWGAN), a novel framework that adaptively learns the intrinsic dimension of data distributions residing on manifolds. LWGAN combines the Wasserstein Auto-encoder (WAE) and Wasserstein GAN (WGAN) to improve generative modeling quality and representation learning by identifying the intrinsic dimension of the data.","methodology":"LWGAN modifies existing GAN and VAE frameworks by changing the latent distribution to a generalized normal distribution N(0, A), where A is a diagonal matrix indicating the intrinsic dimension. It combines WGAN and WAE using a primal-dual iterative algorithm, employing a deterministic encoder Q: X -> Z to learn an informative prior and a generator G: Z -> X to generate realistic images. The 1-Wasserstein distance is used to measure distribution similarities.","experimental_setup":"The framework is validated through simulated experiments on synthetic datasets like S-curves, Swiss rolls, and hyperplanes, as well as benchmark datasets like MNIST and CelebA. Performance is evaluated using visual inspection, inception scores (IS), Fréchet inception distances (FID), and reconstruction errors.","limitations":"The paper assumes the existence of a homeomorphism between the data manifold and a Euclidean space. The 1-Lipschitz constraint on the critic function is enforced using gradient penalty, which might introduce its own set of challenges. The selection of the regularization parameter λn is also a critical issue, and while a data-driven scheme is proposed, its effectiveness might vary across different datasets.","future_research_directions":"Future research directions include investigating a more general scenario where the generator G is stochastic, incorporating stochastic LWGAN into more recent GAN modules like BigGAN to produce high-resolution images while estimating intrinsic dimension, and exploring applications in structural estimation for economic modeling."}

{"arxiv_id":"2402.12376v4","arxiv_url":"http://arxiv.org/abs/2402.12376v4","title":"FiT: Flexible Vision Transformer for Diffusion Model","authors":["Zeyu Lu","Zidong Wang","Di Huang","Chengyue Wu","Xihui Liu","Wanli Ouyang","Lei Bai"],"published_date":"2024-02-19T18:59:07Z","journal":"","doi":"","summary":"Nature is infinitely resolution-free. In the context of this reality,
existing diffusion models, such as Diffusion Transformers, often face
challenges when processing image resolutions outside of their trained domain.
To overcome this limitation, we present the Flexible Vision Transformer (FiT),
a transformer architecture specifically designed for generating images with
unrestricted resolutions and aspect ratios. Unlike traditional methods that
perceive images as static-resolution grids, FiT conceptualizes images as
sequences of dynamically-sized tokens. This perspective enables a flexible
training strategy that effortlessly adapts to diverse aspect ratios during both
training and inference phases, thus promoting resolution generalization and
eliminating biases induced by image cropping. Enhanced by a meticulously
adjusted network structure and the integration of training-free extrapolation
techniques, FiT exhibits remarkable flexibility in resolution extrapolation
generation. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate the exceptional performance
of FiT across a broad range of resolutions, showcasing its effectiveness both
within and beyond its training resolution distribution. Repository available at
https://github.com/whlzy/FiT.","github_url":"https://github.com/whlzy/FiT","main_contributions":"The paper introduces Flexible Vision Transformer (FiT), a novel transformer architecture for diffusion models, enabling image generation at arbitrary resolutions and aspect ratios. Key contributions include a flexible training pipeline that eliminates cropping, a unique transformer architecture for dynamic token length modeling using 2D RoPE, and a training-free resolution extrapolation method.","methodology":"FiT builds upon the Diffusion Transformer (DiT) architecture. It uses a flexible training pipeline that maintains the original image aspect ratio and resizes images to fit within a maximum token limit. The network architecture incorporates 2D Rotary Positional Embedding (RoPE), Swish-Gated Linear Unit (SwiGLU), and Masked Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA). Training-free resolution extrapolation is achieved through modified RoPE interpolation techniques like VisionNTK and VisionYaRN.","experimental_setup":"The model was trained on the ImageNet dataset with a maximum token length of 256. The training used a constant learning rate of 1e-4, AdamW optimizer, and a batch size of 256. Evaluation metrics included Frechet Inception Distance (FID), sFID, Inception Score (IS), Precision, and Recall. Experiments were conducted on various resolutions and aspect ratios, both within and beyond the training distribution.","limitations":"The FiT-XL/2 model was trained for 1.8 million steps, and its performance at 256x256 resolution is slightly inferior compared to DiT-XL/2, which was trained longer. The generative capabilities of FiT-XL/2 were not fully explored with higher resolution training. The exploration of resolution extrapolation techniques was limited to training-free methods.","future_research_directions":"Future research directions include exploring the generative capabilities of FiT with higher resolution training and investigating resolution extrapolation methods that require additional training. The authors also suggest further studies into generating images with arbitrary resolutions and aspect ratios, enabled by FiT."}
